{{Short description|Mathematical Theorem}}

'''Gamas's theorem''' is a result in [[multilinear algebra]] which states the necessary and sufficient conditions for a [[tensor]] symmetrized by an [[Representation theory of the symmetric group|irreducible representation of the symmetric group]] <math>S_n</math> to be zero. It was proven in 1988 by Carlos Gamas.<ref name="Gamas">{{cite journal
|author1=Carlos Gamas
|title=Conditions for a symmetrized decomposable tensor to be zero
|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications
|volume=108
|pages=83–119
|date=1988
|publisher=Elsevier
|doi=10.1016/0024-3795(88)90180-2|doi-access=free
}}</ref> Additional proofs have been given by Pate<ref name="Pate">{{cite journal
|author1=Thomas H. Pate
|title=Immanants and decomposable tensors that symmetrize to zero
|journal=Linear and Multilinear Algebra
|volume=28
|number=3
|pages=175–184
|date=1990
|publisher=Taylor & Francis
|doi=10.1080/03081089008818039}}</ref> and Berget.<ref name="Berget">{{cite journal
|author1=Andrew Berget
|title=A short proof of Gamas's theorem
|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications
|volume=430
|number=2
|pages=791–794
|date=2009
|publisher=Elsevier
|doi=10.1016/j.laa.2008.09.027|s2cid=115172852
|arxiv=0906.4769
}}</ref>

==Statement of the theorem== 

Let <math>V</math> be a finite-dimensional complex [[vector space]] and <math>\lambda</math> be a [[integer partition|partition]] of <math>n</math>. From the representation theory of the symmetric group <math>S_n</math> it is known that the partition <math>\lambda</math> corresponds to an irreducible representation of <math>S_n</math>. Let <math>\chi^{\lambda}</math> be the [[Character (mathematics)|character]] of this representation.  The tensor <math>v_1 \otimes v_2 \otimes \dots \otimes v_n \in V^{\otimes n}</math> symmetrized by <math>\chi^{\lambda}</math> is defined to be 

<math display="block">
\frac{\chi^{\lambda}(e)}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \chi^{\lambda}(\sigma) v_{\sigma(1)} \otimes v_{\sigma(2)} \otimes \dots \otimes v_{\sigma(n)},   
</math>

where <math>e</math> is the identity element of <math>S_n</math>. Gamas's theorem states that the above symmetrized tensor is non-zero if and only if it is possible to partition the set of vectors <math>\{v_i\}</math> into [[Linear independence|linearly independent]] sets whose sizes are in [[bijection]] with the lengths of the columns of the partition <math>\lambda</math>.
